ActionHint.hunt: Hunt a target; gather information about its location and movements; attack with precision shooting from a distance.
ActionHint.study: Study a person, document, or item with close scrutiny to gather information and apply knowledge; gain a deeper understanding; do research.
ActionHint.survey: Survey a location or situation to understand what’s going on; sense trouble before it happens; gather information about opportunities or exploits.
ActionHint.tinker: Tinker with mechanisms to create, modify, disable, or repair; disable a trap, pick a lock, or crack a safe.
ActionHint.finesse: Finesse an item from someone’s pocket; employ subtle misdirection or sleight-of-hand; handle a vehicle or a mount.
ActionHint.prowl: Prowl about unseen and traverse obstacles; climb, swim, run, jump, and tumble. Ambush with close violence.
ActionHint.skirmish: Skirmish with an opponent in close combat; assault or hold a position; brawl and wrestle.
ActionHint.wreck: Wreck a place, item, or obstacle with savage force or carefully applied sabotage; breach defenses with force; create distractions and chaos.
ActionHint.attune: Attune to spirits and the ghost field; channel electroplasmic energy; perceive and communicate with ghosts; understand spectrology.
ActionHint.command: Command obedience with your force of personality; intimidate or threaten; lead an action with one of the crew’s gangs.
ActionHint.consort: Consort with connections from your heritage, background, friends, or rivals to gain access to resources, information, people, or places.
ActionHint.sway: Sway someone with charm, logic, deception, disguise, or bluff; change attitudes or behavior with manipulation or seduction.

Position.label: Position
Position.controlledHint: You act on your terms. You exploit a dominant advantage.
Position.riskyHint: You go head to head. You act under fire. You take a chance.
Position.desperateHint: You overreach your capabilities. You’re in serious trouble.

Outcome.critical: You do it with increased effect.

controlled.partial: You hesitate. Withdraw and try a different approach, or else do it with a minor consequence: a minor complication occurs, you have reduced effect, you suffer lesser harm, you end up in a risky position.
controlled.failure: You falter. Press on by seizing a risky opportunity, or withdraw and try a different approach.

risky.partial: You do it, but there’s a consequence: you suffer harm, a complication occurs, you have reduced effect, you end up in a desperate position.
risky.failure: Things go badly. You suffer harm, a complication occurs, you end up in a desperate position, you lose this opportunity.

desperate.partial: You do it, but there’s a consequence: you suffer severe harm, a serious complication occurs, you have reduced effect.
desperate.failure: It’s the worst outcome. You suffer severe harm, a serious complication occurs, you lose this opportunity for action.

Fortune.title: Fortune Roll
Fortune.hint: Generally 1 to 4 dice, from the trait that applies. Zero dice rolls two and keeps the lowest.
Fortune.critical: Exceptional result: the trait manifests with extreme effect.
Fortune.success: Full effect: the trait manifests strongly.
Fortune.partial: Limited effect: the trait manifests partially.
Fortune.failure: Poor result: the trait barely manifests at all.

Plan.heading: Plan
Plan.detailHint: The one detail the plan needs.

Load.label: Load
Load.lightHint: You look like an ordinary citizen. You’re faster and less conspicuous.
Load.normalHint: You look like a scoundrel, ready for trouble.
Load.heavyHint: You look like an operative on a dangerous mission. You’re slower.
Load.instructions: Choose your load when the score begins. During the score, tick items as you reveal you brought them.
Load.over: You’re carrying more than your load allows.

Cohort.label: Cohorts
Cohort.none: No cohorts yet. A new cohort costs two upgrades.
Cohort.rollHint: Send the cohort to act on its own: roll its quality.
Cohort.brokenWarn: {name} is broken and can’t act until they recover.
Cohort.derived: Quality {quality} from the crew’s Tier. Rolls {pool}d on its own.

Faction.empty: There are no factions in this world yet.

Clock.noneHint: No clocks pinned. Create a clock, or pin one from its sheet.

Payoff.title: Payoff for {name}
Payoff.coin2: 2 coin: minor job; several full purses.
Payoff.coinBonusHint: Add +2 for a claim such as Fixer, Envoy or Loyal Fence if it applies.
Payoff.quiet: Kept completely quiet (no rep, no status changes)
Payoff.repFull: Your rep tracker is full: you earn no rep until you develop.
Payoff.repFullNote: Rep tracker full: no rep earned.
Payoff.overflow: {n} coin won’t fit in the vault and goes to the scoundrels’ stashes.

Heat.crowsVeil: Crow’s Veil: no extra heat for killing.
Heat.wantedUp: Heat filled: wanted level rises to {n}.

arrest.name: Arrest
arrest.text: An Inspector presents a case file of evidence to a magistrate, to begin prosecution of your crew. The Bluecoats send a detail to arrest you. Pay them off with coin (wanted level +3 = {payoff}), hand someone over for arrest (this clears your heat), or try to evade capture.

cooperation.name: Cooperation
cooperation.text: A +3 status faction asks you for a favor. Agree to do it or forfeit 1 rep per Tier of the friendly faction or lose 1 status with them. If you don’t have a +3 faction status, you avoid entanglements right now.

demonicNotice.name: Demonic Notice
demonicNotice.text: A demon approaches the crew with a dark offer. Accept, hide until it loses interest (forfeit 3 rep), or deal with it another way.

flipped.name: Flipped
flipped.text: One of your contacts, patrons, clients, or a group of your customers switches allegiances due to the heat on you. They’re loyal to another faction now.

gangTrouble.name: Gang Trouble
gangTrouble.text: One of your gangs (or other cohorts) causes trouble due to their flaw(s). Lose face (forfeit rep equal to your Tier+1 = {rep}), make an example of one of the gang members, or face reprisals from the wronged party. If you lack a gang or other cohort with a flaw, there’s no entanglement.

interrogation.name: Interrogation
interrogation.text: The Bluecoats round up one of the PCs to question them about the crew’s crimes. How did they manage to capture you? Pay them off with 3 coin, or they beat you up (level 2 harm) and you tell them what they want to know (+3 heat). You can resist each of those consequences separately.

questioning.name: Questioning
questioning.text: The Bluecoats grab an NPC member of your crew or one of the crew’s contacts, to question them about your crimes. Who do the Bluecoats think is most vulnerable? Make a fortune roll to see how much they talk (1-3: +2 heat, 4/5: +1 heat), or pay the Bluecoats off with 2 coin.

reprisals.name: Reprisals
reprisals.text: An enemy faction makes a move against you (or a friend, contact, or vice purveyor). Pay them (1 rep and 1 coin) per Tier of the enemy as an apology, allow them to mess with you or yours, or fight back and show them who’s boss.

rivals.name: Rivals
rivals.text: A neutral faction throws their weight around. They threaten you, a friend or contact, or one of your vice purveyors. Forfeit (1 rep or 1 coin) per Tier of the rival, or stand up to them and lose 1 status with them.

showOfForce.name: Show of Force
showOfForce.text: A faction with whom you have a negative status makes a play against your holdings. Give them 1 claim or go to war (drop to -3 status). If you have no claims, lose 1 hold instead.

unquietDead.name: Unquiet Dead
unquietDead.text: A rogue spirit is drawn to you (perhaps it’s a past victim?). Acquire the services of a Whisper or Rail Jack to attempt to destroy or banish it, or deal with it yourself.

usualSuspects.name: The Usual Suspects
usualSuspects.text: The Bluecoats grab someone in the periphery of your crew. One player volunteers a friend or vice purveyor as the person most likely to be taken. Make a fortune roll to find out if they resist questioning (1-3: +2 heat, 4/5: level 2 harm), or pay the Bluecoats off with 1 coin.

Downtime.label: Downtime
Downtime.title: {name}: {activity}
Downtime.acquireHint: A carriage, a gang of thugs for the night, a forged warrant…
Downtime.heatHint: How do you reduce the heat on the crew?
Downtime.acquireExplain: Roll the crew’s Tier ({n}). 1-3 inferior (Tier-1), 4/5 standard (Tier), 6 fine (Tier+1), critical exceptional (Tier+2).
Downtime.bumpHint: After the roll you may spend coin to raise the result, one level per coin.
Downtime.acquireResult: You acquire an asset of quality {q}.
Downtime.recoverHealed: {n} ticks: the healing clock fills. Each harm is reduced by one level.
Downtime.noClockPermission: You can’t create actors: ask the GM to make the project clock. The ticks are reported on the card.
Downtime.extraExplain: You’ve used your free downtime activities. Each extra activity costs 1 coin or 1 rep.
Downtime.cohortsMend: Cohorts recover one level of harm.
Downtime.activities: Each scoundrel has {n} free downtime activities.
Downtime.crewHint: The GM opens downtime: armor resets, cohorts mend, and income claims pay out. Scoundrels take their activities from their own sheets.

Vice.title: {name} indulges their vice
Vice.explain: Roll your lowest attribute ({n}d) and clear stress equal to the highest die. You have {stress} {label}. Clear more than you have and you overindulge.
Vice.overindulgedHint: You make a bad call because of your vice. Choose one:
Vice.attractTroubleHint: Select or roll an additional entanglement.
Vice.bragHint: You brag about your exploits. +2 heat.
Vice.lostHint: You vanish on a bender. Play a different character until this one returns.
Vice.tappedHint: Your current purveyor cuts you off. Find a new source for your vice.

Xp.label: XP
Xp.desperate: Every time you roll a desperate action, mark xp in that action’s attribute.
Xp.endNote: At the end of each session, for each item below, mark 1 xp (in your playbook or an attribute) or 2 xp if that item occurred multiple times.
Xp.sessionHint: For each trigger, mark 1 if it happened, 2 if it happened a lot.

Advance.title: {name} takes an advance
Advance.crewHint: Take a new crew ability, or mark two upgrade boxes.

Develop.notFull: The rep tracker isn’t full yet.
Develop.paid: Paid {n} coin. Hold is now weak.

Harm.label: Harm
Harm.healingHint: Tick during downtime recovery. When it fills, each harm drops a level.
Harm.needHelpWarn: Severe harm: you can’t act unless helped or you push yourself.
Harm.lessEffectNote: Lesser harm: effect reduced one level.

Armor.title: Use armor
Armor.explain: Mark an armor box to reduce or avoid the consequence without rolling.
Armor.usedHint: The consequence is reduced or avoided.

Trauma.title: {name} suffers {label}
Trauma.explain: {name}’s stress track is full. Clear stress, mark a {label} condition, and leave the scene.
Trauma.out: Out of action for the rest of this scene.
Trauma.retire: That is the last trauma. The character must retire.

Resist.title: {name} resists
Resist.attrHint: Insight for deception and understanding; Prowess for physical strain and injury; Resolve for mental strain and willpower.
Resist.explain: Resistance always works: the consequence is reduced or avoided. You take 6 minus your highest die in {label}.
Resist.outcome: The consequence is reduced or avoided.

Roll.goalHint: What are you trying to do?
Roll.pushHarm: Push yourself to act despite severe harm (2 {label})
Roll.pushHarmNote: Pushed to act despite severe harm.
Roll.noCharacter: Assign yourself a scoundrel (User Configuration), or select a scoundrel’s token, to do that.

Group.already: You’ve already joined this group action.
Group.leaderStress: The leader takes {n} {label}, one for each failure.
Group.noStress: No failures: no stress for the leader.

Engagement.title: Engagement roll
Engagement.hint: 1d for sheer luck. +1d for each major advantage (a bold plan, a vulnerable target, friends helping), -1d for each major disadvantage (a well-defended target, enemies in the way).
Engagement.abilitiesHint: Add bonus dice for abilities and claims that apply (Predators, Cover Identities, City Records…).
Engagement.claimBonus: +1d from a claim for this plan.
Engagement.criticalHint: You’ve already overcome the first obstacle and you’re in a controlled position for what’s next.
Engagement.successHint: You’re in a controlled position when the action starts.
Engagement.partialHint: You’re in a risky position when the action starts.
Engagement.failureHint: You’re in a desperate position when the action starts.

Flashback.title: {name}: flashback
Flashback.cost0: an ordinary action with easy opportunity
Flashback.cost1: a complex action or unlikely opportunity
Flashback.cost2: an elaborate action with special opportunities or contingencies
Flashback.hint: If the flashback action is challenging, roll for it as usual.

Call.title: Call for a roll
Call.kicker: The GM calls for a roll
Call.goalHint: What are they trying to do?

Score.freeHint: Choose a target, gather information, decide on the plan.
Score.afterHint: Payoff, heat, then entanglements, in that order.

Crew.name: Crew name
Crew.turfBox: Turf: rep you no longer need to develop.
Crew.membersHint: Drop a scoundrel here, or choose this crew on their sheet.
Crew.advanceStash: Each time the crew advances, each scoundrel gets stash equal to Tier+2.
Crew.warHint: At war: +1 heat from scores, hold drops by one, and only one free downtime activity.
Crew.contactsHint: Mark your favourite contact with the triangle.
Crew.huntingHint: On your hunting grounds, operations of your preferred type get +1d to gather information and a free downtime activity towards them.
Crew.deityHint: Alluring, Cruel, Ferocious, Monstrous, Radiant, Sinister, Serene, Transcendent
Crew.none: There is no crew yet. Create a Crew actor.

CrewType.dropHint: Drag a crew type here from the Crew Types compendium.
CrewType.dragHint: Drag onto a crew sheet to apply it.

Claims.label: Claims
Claims.offPath: {name} doesn’t connect to anything you hold. Seizing it off the roadmap takes exceptional effort. Mark it anyway?

Upgrade.costs: New cohort: 2 upgrades. Add a type: 2 upgrades.
Upgrade.carriageHint: A carriage, two goats to pull it, and a stable. A second upgrade adds armor and larger, swifter goats.
Upgrade.boatHint: A boat, a dock on a waterway, and a shack for boating supplies. A second upgrade adds armor and cargo capacity.
Upgrade.hiddenHint: Your lair has a secret location and is disguised to hide it from view.
Upgrade.quartersHint: Living quarters for the crew. Without them, each PC sleeps elsewhere, and is vulnerable when they do.
Upgrade.secureHint: Locks, alarms and traps. A second upgrade adds arcane measures against spirits.
Upgrade.vaultHint: Storage for coin rises to 8; a second upgrade raises it to 16. Part of it can serve as a holding cell.
Upgrade.workshopHint: Tools for tinkering and alchemy, and a small library: long-term projects without leaving the lair.
Upgrade.vehicleHint: Your vehicle. A second upgrade gives it armor.
Upgrade.insightHint: Mark 2 xp (not 1) when you train Insight.
Upgrade.prowessHint: Mark 2 xp (not 1) when you train Prowess.
Upgrade.resolveHint: Mark 2 xp (not 1) when you train Resolve.
Upgrade.personalHint: Mark 2 xp (not 1) when you train your playbook.
Upgrade.masteryHint: Action ratings may advance to 4. Costs four upgrade boxes.
Upgrade.gearHint: +1 quality for burglary and climbing gear.
Upgrade.toolsHint: +1 quality for demolition and tinkering tools.

Sheet.name: Name
Sheet.ratingCap: Action ratings can’t go above {n} yet. The crew’s Mastery upgrade raises the limit to 4.
Sheet.ratingCapGM: Action ratings can’t go above {n} yet: the crew needs the Mastery upgrade. Shift-click to override.
Sheet.lockedDot: Locked until the crew has the Mastery upgrade

Playbook.dropHint: Drag a playbook here from the Playbooks compendium.
Playbook.dragHint: Drag onto a scoundrel to apply it: abilities, items, friends and starting actions.

Gear.toggleHint: Tick when you reveal you brought it.

Friends.label: Friends
Friends.hint: Mark one close friend (▲) and one rival (▼).

Drop.crewOnly: That belongs on a crew sheet.
Drop.scoundrelOnly: That belongs on a scoundrel’s sheet.

toolbar.name: Show the Blades toolbar
toolbar.hint: A small toolbar under the scene controls with clocks, factions, rolls and rules.

clocksOnLoad.name: Open the clocks panel on load
clocksOnLoad.hint: Show pinned clocks when the world loads.
